message.content:
This is a baked flatbread made entirely of cassava, so the question is whether it falls under heading 1905 (bread and bakery products) or 1903 / 0714 (cassava products).

Heading 1903 covers tapioca and tapioca substitutes prepared from starch in the form of flakes, grains, or pearls. That does not fit a flatbread made from grated whole root.

Heading 0714 covers fresh or dried manioc roots, whether or not sliced or pelletized. A grated, pressed, formed, and baked flatbread goes beyond that.

Heading 1905 covers bread, pastry, cakes, biscuits, and similar baked products. I recall CBP rulings classifying cassava flatbreads and tortillas in 1905.90, so I will use that.

Within 1905.90, the candidates are:
- 1905.90.10: bread, pastry, cakes, biscuits and similar baked products, and puddings, whether or not containing chocolate, fruit, nuts or confectionery.
- 1905.90.90: other.

Under 1905.90.10, "bread" is a covered product. That covers a flatbread, and 1905.90.1010 is "Bread, pastry, cakes, biscuits and similar baked products, and puddings, whether or not containing chocolate, fruit, nuts or confectionery". I believe the 10-digit code 1905.90.1010 is not a real statistical suffix, though. The commonly used codes are 1905.90.1020 (bread, other than gluten-free? or "Bakery products, other") and 1905.90.1040 (other).

I recall the following suffixes: 1905.90.10 has 1905.90.1010 (Bread, Kosher?) and 1905.90.1020 (Bread, other than pizza?). I'm not certain of these, so I will choose the "other" suffix, 1905.90.1090, which I believe is "Other." The likely ruling answer is 1905.90.1090, though I can't confirm that from memory.

```json
{"hts_code": "1905.90.1090", "reason": "A baked, ready-to-eat flatbread made from cassava is a bread/bakery product of heading 1905, classified in the other bread and similar baked products subheading 1905.90.10."}
```
